kind: STALE WORKTREE TRIAGE -- inspects and reports, never edits

item_2_modified_tracked_files.disposition: UNRESOLVED BY THIS SCRIPT, ON PURPOSE. The PI ruled on gpu-sim-u2o.6.6.2 that the v8 family files stay exactly as found and are dispositioned under this bead. Committing them requires regenerating metrics.json from a MIXED set (v8 memory/reduce/gemm beside v6 launch), which is the very mixed-provenance artifact this bead exists to prevent. Resetting them discards three finished GPU jobs. Both need the PI's word, so neither is done here.

item_3_untracked_paths.CORRECTION: The bead's design -- and my own earlier report on gpu-sim-u2o.6.6.2 -- says TWO of the master-owned copies differ (harness.md, preflight_validator.py). MEASURED, it is 20 of 34, all under epic_u2o/. Those two files really are in the set; they are not the only ones. I had confirmed two examples and reported the number of examples as the total, which understates the hazard by an order of magnitude -- twenty stale copies of master-owned code is a different problem from two.
item_3_untracked_paths.assertion: no untracked path in the worktree may also be tracked in master; the collisions list above is the evidence, and it is currently NON-EMPTY
item_3_untracked_paths.why_it_matters: a bulk `git add` in that worktree would add 34 files master already owns, and any branch switch there would overwrite them -- the rebase earlier refused for exactly this reason.

item_4_mechanism.problem: queue jobs wrote artifacts into a live worktree while git operations were available in the same tree; a tracked-path restore there replaced a finished job's output 20 seconds after it was written
item_4_mechanism.what_this_bead_adds: measure_family.py stamps every artifact with its writing job id and a content hash, and verify_artifact_provenance.py compares on-disk provenance against the queue's own record -- so the restore is detectable rather than silent. That is detection, not prevention; prevention is item 4's open question of where jobs should write.
item_4_mechanism.open: item 4 also asks that a worktree be QUIESCED before a git operation that can touch tracked paths. That is enforced for destructive git by scripts/guard_destructive_git.py (gpu-sim-edu.1.1 / edu.2), which now also refuses anything that would delete the lab runtime. It is NOT yet enforced for non-destructive tracked-path writes, and this script does not pretend otherwise.
